newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: HK's Hutchison retains Philippine port deal.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hutchison retains Philippine port deal.

text.p: Approval for a unit of Hong Kong's Hutchison Whampoa to develop and operate a container port at a former U.S. naval base in the Philippines has been upheld following a re-evaluation of the bidding.

The Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority, which runs the port at the former base north of Manila, said on Tuesday it had re-evaluated all bids for the project and decided Hutchison Ports Philippines Ltd still came out the winner.
"The decision is subject to review by President Fidel Ramos, to whom it has been submitted," an SBMA statement said.
SBMA initially awarded the contract to Hutchison, but the decision was challenged by one of the losing bidders, Philippine port operator International Container Terminal Services Inc (ICTSI).

Ramos ordered SBMA to re-evaluate the bidding, and today's announcement was the result of that review, which SBMA said was conducted with observers from the Philippine government's Commission on Audit.
ICTSI immediately said it was prepared to challenge the latest ruling, up to the Supreme Court if necessary.
"We still have the option of going to the Supreme Court. We can't think about that until we're there. We'll take it step by step," ICTSI chairman Enrique Razon told Reuters.

SBMA rejected ICTSI's original bid on the grounds that it would violate a law forbidding monopolies in the port industry. ICTSI operates the Manila International Container Terminal, which handles 70 percent of container traffic in the country.
But in its review, SBMA said it had based its decision purely on the financial returns each of the competing bidders had offered.
"This greatest financial return is not an arbitrary figure quoted by the bidder but should be supported by a valid or realistic business plan," SBMA said in a statement.
It said it rejected ICTSI's contention that the only financial factor that should be looked into was royalty per twenty-foot-equivalent unit (TEU).
In the original bidding in August, ICTSI offered the highest royalty of $58 per TEU, followed by Hutchison with $20.50 and Germany's Royal Port Services with $15.00.

In its bid, Hutchison said it planned to build new wharfs at Subic in the fourth year that would effectively increase the number of ship calls at a faster pace. It also pledged to invest more than $100 million in Subic over a 10-year period.
ICTSI had set the construction of new wharfs only in the ninth year and had promised fresh investment of $79 million, according to documents provided by the SBMA.
ICTSI had offered a higher royalty because it would raise its rates and charges by 10 percent yearly for the first two years and 5.0 percent thereafter, the SBMA said.
SBMA said it had hired three independent experts from Malaysia, Belgium and the United States who also endorsed the Hutchison plan.
Subic used to be the biggest American naval base outside the United States. It was closed after the Philippine Senate refused to agree to a new treaty with Washington in 1991.
It is now a flourishing economic development zone.
